items.quote: The Grain API lets you read and manage recordings, highlights, uploads, and more.
items.why: Quote covers recordings, highlights, uploads. No transcripts, webhooks, or 'meeting recorder' wording.

items.quote: The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension
items.why: Supports oauth2 only. No bearer_token mention.

items.quote: At least one redirect URI is required to register a new client.
items.why: Redirect URI registration rule. Says nothing about auth methods.

items.quote: Public clients, such as MCP clients and native apps, can skip Step 1 by using an HTTPS URL as their client_id.
items.why: HTTPS client_id skip for public clients. Detail only, not the method list.

items.quote: The `workspace` scope is only available to clients verified by Grain.
items.why: Workspace scope verification gate. Not admin approval, and only for one scope.

items.quote: Available on every plan, including Free.
items.why: Says PAT available on all plans. Cuts against an admin-approval gate.

items.quote: Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans.
items.why: Admin access plus Business/Enterprise gate. Covers only the WAT, not all credentials.

items.quote: The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events
items.why: Generic capability blurb. No REST, no breadth list, no version details.

items.quote: The API allows 300 requests per minute per token.
items.why: Supports the 300/min rate limit only. Per-token scope matches.
Exact integration URL shown. Vendor-official status not shown in quote.

items.quote: Any MCP client that can send custom headers can connect with a Personal Access Token instead of OAuth.
items.why: Implies MCP client connections exist. Does not prove vendor-official or the URL.
